output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: extractFile validated only the *location* of an extracted entry (targetFileName) against the destination directory, never the *target* of a symlink entry. A crafted tar/zip with a symlink whose link name is an absolute (or ../-traversing) path outside the destination caused SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(targetFileName, new File(symlinkDestination)) to create a symlink escaping the destination — an arbitrary read/write primitive.

Fix (AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile): after the existing target-location containment check, when symlinkDestination is non-empty, resolve the link target — absolute targets as-is, relative targets against the symlink's parent directory — canonicalize it, and throw ArchiverException("Entry symlink destination is outside of the target directory (...)") unless it startsWith the canonical destination directory. Because both TarUnArchiver and AbstractZipUnArchiver feed symlinkDestination into this single sink, one check covers both trace paths from the alert.

Tests: the shared fixture src/test/resources/symlinks/src intentionally contains symlinks pointing outside the archive root (../onTheOutside.txt, ../dirOnTheOutside/), so the pre-existing SymlinkTest.testSymlinkTar/testSymlinkZip (which extracted that fixture) now correctly reject it — updated them to assertThrows(ArchiverException) with a message check. Added testSymlinkWithinDestinationIsExtracted to prove an in-bounds symlink (symR -> fileR.txt) still extracts successfully, preserving positive coverage.

Verification: POV (bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh) exit 0 → 2 after patch (extraction rejects the escaping symlink). Full suite: 322 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 10 skipped (skip count unchanged from baseline). SymlinkTest: 7 run, 0 failures.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavior change: extracting archives that contain symlinks whose destinations point outside the extraction directory now throws ArchiverException instead of silently creating an escaping symlink. This is stricter than current upstream plexus-archiver (which permits such symlinks and only guards subsequent same-extraction writes via canonical-path checks). Consumers who legitimately rely on archives producing symlinks that escape the destination (uncommon; also the exploit vector) will now get an exception. Relative symlinks resolving within the destination, and symlinks to files inside it, are unaffected. Containment uses getCanonicalFile().toPath().startsWith(canonicalDir); the symlink target need not exist yet (canonicalization normalizes the non-existent suffix), consistent with the existing entry-location check.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 symlink-escape in plexus-archiver: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile now validates that a symbolic-link entry's destination resolves within the extraction directory, rejecting archive-created symlinks that escape it. This closes both the tar (TarUnArchiver.getLinkName) and zip (AbstractZipUnArchiver.resolveSymlink) flows, which share the same extractFile sink.
